title: Community invited to greet Vietnam veterans returning from Honor Flight
summary: Saints Simon and Jude Parish hosts a Welcome Home celebration on Saturday, Sept. 19 for Vietnam veterans coming back from Honor Flight Philadelphia's Day of Honor in Washington. Activities start at 4 p.m. and the buses arrive around 6 p.m.; organizers are asking neighbors to line the entrance with flags.
loc: Saints Simon and Jude Parish, West Chester

title: West Chester University marks 25 years since 9/11 with three days of tributes
summary: A student-veteran memorial ceremony opens Friday, Sept. 11 at 9 a.m. on the Academic Quad with remarks from West Chester Police Chief Josh Lee, followed that evening by the 10th annual Concert on the Quad from the Wells School of Music. Saturday's football opener against IUP adds a film tribute to alumnus Michael Horrocks, co-pilot of United Flight 175, and post-game fireworks. All events are free.
loc: West Chester University, 700 S. High Street, West Chester

title: Westtown School breaks ground on a $29M dining and community center
summary: The Quaker school is midway through a run of campus construction, having finished a $10.9 million athletic complex with two lighted synthetic turf fields and a seven-acre solar array that covers up to 91% of campus electricity. Now underway is a $29 million all-electric dining and community center beside the historic Main Building, the centerpiece of a $62 million campaign.

title: A speakeasy-style barbershop opens down an alley off High Street
summary: Gerome and Monica Ruff have opened Urban Cutz Barbershop at 21 S. High Street, tucked behind Ginkgo Arts and reached through a covered brick walkway next to Barnaby's. Gerome has cut hair in the borough for more than 18 years; the couple plan to add chairs and more barbers as the 1,200-square-foot shop grows.

title: Free veterans documentary screening at WCU on Sept. 10
summary: West Chester University's Veterans Center and the Chester County Suicide Prevention Partnership are showing The Journey Home, local filmmaker Gary Chilutti's documentary on veterans returning to civilian life with PTSD, Sept. 10 from 6 to 8:30 p.m. The screening at the Madeleine Wing Adler Theatre is free and open to the public, followed by a community conversation.

title: Community-owned grocery store opens on West Market Street
summary: The West Chester Co-op opened Aug. 21 at 204 W. Market Street after more than a decade of organizing, fundraising and volunteer work, giving the borough a walkable grocery option again. The 2,800-square-foot market is open 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. daily and stocks local produce, dairy and baked goods alongside everyday staples; membership has passed 830.

title: QVC Group cuts two president roles as post-bankruptcy shakeup continues
summary: HSN president Stacy Bowe and chief growth officer Alex Wellen both leave the West Chester home-shopping company Sept. 4, and their president positions are being eliminated outright. The move follows QVC's Chapter 11 restructuring and the August departure of CEO David Rawlinson II, with predecessor Mike George back on an interim basis.

title: Fantasy bookstore Leaves & Lore nearly sells out in its first weekend
summary: The father-daughter shop at 118 N. High Street opened Aug. 22 to a line that held steady for six hours, filling 600 orders and drawing about 1,500 people on day one before closing early Sunday on low stock. Jeffrey and Jessie Hilker spent two years finding the storefront, the former home of arts-and-crafts store Nightingale Materials.

title: Borough tightens the rules on where smoke and vape shops can open
summary: Borough Council voted unanimously Aug. 19 to allow new smoke and vape shops only by conditional use in the town center and commercial services district, after a corner store on a residential block reopened as a vape shop. New shops must sit more than 500 feet from schools, day cares, libraries and bus stops; the five or so existing shops downtown are unaffected.

title: Christkindlmarkt sets a Dec. 12 date with 100-plus vendors downtown
summary: The seventh annual holiday market returns Saturday, Dec. 12 from 11 a.m. to 6 p.m., filling Gay Street between Darlington and Matlack and Church Street between Gay and Chestnut with more than 100 artists, makers and food vendors. The West Chester Downtown Foundation runs it with the Chester County Art Association and Downtown West Chester; admission is free, rain or shine.
loc: Gay and Church streets, West Chester
